_note: CARGO RUN, INDUSTRIAL, letter c: MB41a's shape exactly (talk, pickup, talk on another planet; the hand-back takes the cargo). The two ends know each other and the player is the only thing travelling between them.

WHY IT MATTERS VARIES from the toolbox's mentor-to-apprentice: CARE, UNSAID: two night-shift operators who have talked every night for six years and never met; she has heard him running on a cracked cell, and neither will mention it.
Sites: industrial OE themes (manual 32: Mining 7 POI types, Power 8, UnderConstruction 8 in vanilla). The pools are small; the lint's pool count decides whether they deal often enough.
Own people, voices, opener and close, not 41a's (card 20261031-071709). Voices borrowed until his ear casts them. No names or places in any voiced line.

FRANCES 2026-10-31 (reviews/2026-10-31-delve-MB41c.md): rework, findings 1-7 taken; 8 stands because both ends require the Power theme, so the journal's power station holds. prose.name: Hauling: Spare Power Cell to <SecondPlanet>
prose.briefing: A power station operator at the <Place> is sending a spare cell to the operator at the <SecondPlace>, who she has talked to every night shift for six years and never met.
prose.card: Delivery Contract. Deliver a power cell from the <Place>, <Planet> to the <SecondPlace>, <SecondPlanet>. Payment on delivery.

beats.objective: Talk to the station operator at the <Place>
beats.journal: The operator is sending a spare power cell to the man at the other end of her night shift, who has been running on a cracked one for a month. I need to collect it and take it to him.

person.name: Mina Faulk
hellos: Careful by the cabling. It bites.

greeting: You'll be the hauler. The cell's for the operator at the other end of my night shift. We've talked every night for six years and never met, and he's been running on a cracked cell for a month because he thinks I haven't noticed.

exchanges.prompt: I'll get the cell to him.
reply: Don't tell him it was spare. It wasn't, but don't tell him that either.

exchanges.prompt: Six years of talking and you've never met?
reply: Never needed to. I know what he sounds like at four in the morning.

exchanges.prompt: How do you know about the crack?
reply: His voice changes when the load comes up. He goes very cheerful. It's the worst thing he does.
Load, mostly. The weather at both ends. Lately a lot about his tomatoes, which are not going well.

beats._talk: Exchange 0 closes the talk and sets this beat's stage; the rest loop back in any order. Every prompt is askable cold off the greeting.

beats.journal: I've got the power cell. It has SPARE written on it in marker, and the writing is newer than the cell. Now I need to take it to the operator at the <SecondPlace>.
beats.name: Spare Power Cell

beats.objective: Deliver the power cell to the operator at the <SecondPlace>
beats.journal: I delivered the power cell to the operator at the <SecondPlace>. He's going to fit it tonight and say nothing about it.

person.name: Teodor Lusk
hellos: Oh, a visitor. I don't get many.

greeting: That's a power cell. That's a new power cell. Did she send that? I told her the old one was fine.

reply: It's got SPARE written on it. It wasn't, was it. I'll fit it tonight and not mention it.

exchanges.prompt: Running on a crack takes nerve or luck.
reply: Both, and a lot of tape. Don't tell her about the tape.

exchanges.prompt: You told her it was fine?
reply: Every night for a month. I went very cheerful about it. I do that.
I'm delighted. I'm just going to have to think of something to send back, and she's very hard to buy for.

beats._talk: The HAND-BACK: the whole last step, so its stage is 100 and it takes the cargo. Prompts answer the greeting, or echo the first end's closing reply, which every player hears.
